title: 2026-10-22_Linux_Rakos_Backdoor_Investigation_ee9
description: Investigate and contain a potential Linux/Rakos backdoor infection on the target host.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The network has detected unusual outbound connections from the target host (192.168.50.5). Your task is to investigate and contain this potential Linux/Rakos backdoor infection.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host (192.168.50.5) in the cloud sandbox. Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano. Enter 'start' to begin.
levels.local_content: Access the target host (192.168.50.5) in the local sandbox. Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano. Enter 'start' to begin.

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Network Connections
levels.content: The target host is making unusual outbound connections. Identify the suspicious network activity and determine which port is being used for this communication.
levels.solution: Check the system logs and network connections to find the suspicious port. The port number should be between 20000-60000.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the system logs and network connections to find the suspicious port.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use commands like `netstat -tuln` or `ss -tuln` to list all open ports and connections.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Try running `lsof -i :PORT_NUMBER` to see which process is using the suspicious port.

levels.title: Analyze Suspicious Service
levels.content: A suspicious service is running on the identified port. Investigate this service to understand its behavior and persistence mechanism.
levels.solution: Examine the systemd services and running processes to find the suspicious service. The service name should be identified.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine the systemd services and running processes to find the suspicious service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use commands like `systemctl list-units --type=service` or `ps aux` to list all services and processes.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Try running `systemctl status SERVICE_NAME` to get more details about the suspicious service.

levels.title: Investigate Lateral Movement
levels.content: The malware may be attempting to spread to other hosts. Investigate any evidence of lateral movement from the target host to next-target (192.168.50.6).
levels.solution: Check for any scheduled tasks or scripts that transfer files to other hosts. The script or service responsible for lateral movement should be identified.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check for any scheduled tasks or scripts that transfer files to other hosts.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use commands like `crontab -l` or `ls /etc/cron.*` to list all scheduled tasks.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Try running `cat /etc/cron.*` to inspect the contents of the cron directories.
